plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Cisco ASA, ASA Virtual, and Secure Firewall. It reports uptime, CPU utilization, memory utilization, sessions/connections, and interface traffic (enterprise PEN 9).
name: Firewall

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: This metric reports the CPU utilization of the Cisco ASA / Secure Firewall control plane as a 5-minute average (CISCO-PROCESS-MIB cpmCPUTotal5minRev). Sustained high CPU usage can indicate inspection overload or attack traffic and may slow management response.

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage_1min
metrics.description: Optional 1-minute CPU utilization of the Cisco firewall (CISCO-PROCESS-MIB cpmCPUTotal1minRev). Use it when a shorter window than the 5-minute revised average is needed.

metrics.name: device_memory_used
metrics.description: Bytes currently in use in each Cisco memory pool (CISCO-MEMORY-POOL-MIB ciscoMemoryPoolUsed). The MEMPOOL_GLOBAL_SHARED pool is dropped because it dominates ASA memory accounting and is not useful for capacity alerts.

metrics.name: device_memory_free
metrics.description: Free bytes in each Cisco memory pool (CISCO-MEMORY-POOL-MIB ciscoMemoryPoolFree), excluding MEMPOOL_GLOBAL_SHARED. Together with used bytes this is the branch-2 memory model for utilization.

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: Per-pool memory utilization of the Cisco firewall, computed as used / (used + free) * 100 after dropping MEMPOOL_GLOBAL_SHARED. High utilization on Processor or System pools can degrade session handling.

metrics.name: firewall_active_sessions

dimensions.name: index
dimensions.description: SNMP table row index (service.type; type=6 is current in use)

metrics.description: Number of connections currently in use on the Cisco firewall (CISCO-FIREWALL-MIB cfwConnectionStatValue). The table is indexed by service + type; only current-in-use rows (type=6) are kept. A rapid rise can indicate a connection flood or session-table pressure.
